notes: s_getpc_b64 at word 4 yields the address of word 5; +0x14 bytes = word 10. s_swappc_b64 (word 8) jumps to word 10 with return address word 9; words 10-16 compute; s_setpc_b64 s[8:9] (word 17) returns to word 9; s_branch 8 at word 9 goes to word 18 = the end of the body (first post line). All control targets stay in [4,18], computed relative to the PC, so the inlined copy behaves identically.
Branch targets equal to the body end land on the first post instruction, so post must directly follow the words (as the template does).
Results 0..3 are v4..v7 (add 0x13579bdf, xor 0xa5a5a5a5, v6+v7, xor 0x5a5a5a5a); post copies them to v10..v13. All four asserted for every lane.
Rows: Run() sets Input[tid*4..+3] = {Selectors[tid % 8], 0x9e3779b9*(tid+1), 0xffffffff - tid, 17*tid + 1}; Selectors = {0,1,2,3,4,7,0x80000000,0xffffffff}.
The test dispatches one wave of 32 lanes and one of 64 lanes (and a 64-lane dispatch on a wave32 target when distinct). The .wave64 file covers the 64-lane run.
verified: disassembly (llvm-mc gfx1030) of the whole kernel; every PC-relative target computed by hand from the word offsets; Run()/Check()/Expected() read.
